title: Lanthanide-containing clusters for catalytic water splitting and CO2 conversion
claim: Heterometallic Ln–Zn and Ln–Co complexes copolymerize CO2 and cyclohexene oxide by chain shuttling: Lewis-acidic Ln binds the epoxide, a labile Zn- or Co-bound acetate/carbonate opens the ring, and the resulting Ln-alkoxide inserts into Zn-bound CO2 to grow the polycarbonate.
explanation: The review judges heterobimetallic complexes generally superior to homometallic lanthanide initiators for this copolymerization. Examples include Nd2Zn (TOF 82 h−1, Mn about 295800 g mol−1, 99% carbonate) and NdCo3 (TOF 1625 h−1, narrow PDI 1.04). Early homometallic Lu and Dy clusters can be selective but often give broad molecular-weight distributions.
scope: Heterometallic Ln–Zn/Co complexes, including macrocyclic tris(salen) and hexoxime systems, for alternating CO2/cyclohexene oxide copolymerization.
conditions: Varies widely, for example Nd2Zn at 70 °C and 0.7 MPa, and NdCo3 at 130 °C and 2 MPa.
caveats: High carbonate selectivity does not imply a narrow PDI; several homometallic and Y4Zn2 entries have PDIs from about 2 to 9.8. One ligand family that is less active for cycloaddition can still copolymerize.
